input:
This example works through the calculation of the log-mean temperature difference for a countercurrent heat exchanger that cools a process stream from 160 °C to 120 °C, with cooling water entering at 40 °C and leaving at 75 °C.

The terminal temperature differences at the two ends are established first. At the end where the process stream enters, the terminal difference $\Delta T_1$ is 85 K, the difference between the entering process stream at 160 °C and the leaving water at 75 °C. At the opposite end, where the process stream leaves, the terminal difference $\Delta T_2$ is 80 K, the difference between the leaving process stream at 120 °C and the entering water at 40 °C. Countercurrent flow maintains a temperature difference between the streams at every point along the exchanger, and the two terminal differences are quite close, because the temperature changes of the two streams are broadly similar in magnitude.

$$\Delta T_{lm} = \frac{\Delta T_1 - \Delta T_2}{\ln(\Delta T_1 / \Delta T_2)}$$

In this relation, $\Delta T_{lm}$ denotes the log-mean temperature difference, while $\Delta T_1$ and $\Delta T_2$ denote the terminal differences at the two ends of the exchanger. Substituting the terminal differences into the relation gives $\Delta T_{lm}$ = 82.5 K. In practice, heat-exchanger rating uses the log-mean temperature difference as the mean driving force for the unit as a whole, rather than a local difference.

The log-mean temperature difference is valid for an exchanger in which the overall coefficient remains constant along the length and neither stream changes phase. If either stream changes phase, or if the coefficient varies with temperature, the calculation moves outside the conditions under which the relation holds, and the exchanger must instead be rated in sections. The value of 82.5 K lies between the terminal differences of 85 K and 80 K. A mean of the two end differences must lie between them, and the log-mean value sits close to the arithmetic mean because the two terminal differences are close to each other.
